channel.title: AWS CDK Reference Architectures
channel.description: Newly published and newly deploy-verified AWS CDK reference architectures.

item.title: ALB OIDC Authentication with Keycloak on ECS Fargate + Aurora Serverless
item.description: AWS ALB built-in OIDC authentication backed by Keycloak running on ECS Fargate with Aurora Serverless V2 (PostgreSQL) as the session store. Two patterns: Pattern A uses Keycloak as a direct OIDC provider; Pattern B adds SAML identity brokering so Keycloak acts as both an OIDC provider to ALB and a SAML service provider to a corporate IdP. Includes setup scripts for realm/client configuration and ECS Exec enabled for connection testing.

item.title: FIS Chaos: SQS + Lambda Event-Driven Consumer + DynamoDB
item.description: Three AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for a serverless event-driven consumer, using the aws:lambda:function action family via the FIS Lambda extension: a 5-min invocation-error outage (short recovery), a 20-min invocation-error outage (forces DLQ routing past the visibility-timeout × maxReceiveCount threshold), and a 10-min invocation-add-delay throughput collapse — each with a CloudWatch Alarm stop condition on queue backlog depth.

item.title: FIS Chaos: Step Functions Saga + Lambda + DynamoDB
item.description: Three AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for a Saga-pattern order workflow (Reserve Inventory → Process Payment → Confirm Order, each with Retry/Catch and compensating transactions): payment-step outage triggering inventory-release compensation, first-step outage with no compensation needed, and final-step outage triggering the two-stage refund-then-release compensation chain — each with a CloudWatch Alarm stop condition on Step Functions ExecutionsFailed. Uses the aws:lambda:function action family (invocation-error) via the FIS Lambda extension to drive Saga error handling indirectly, since FIS has no native Step Functions action.

item.title: FIS Chaos: Multi-AZ Network Disruption — NLB + EC2 ASG + Aurora
item.description: Four AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for a Multi-AZ resilient architecture: cross-AZ connectivity disruption (VPC-internal traffic only), full AZ isolation (all traffic blocked), Aurora writer→reader failover, and tagged EC2 instance termination — each with a CloudWatch Alarm stop condition on NLB UnHealthyHostCount. Centers on aws:network:disrupt-connectivity, the only FIS action for simulating AZ-level network partitions.

item.title: FIS Chaos: ARC Zonal Shift on Auto Scaling
item.description: A direct follow-up to Architecture G's G-2 finding (Auto Scaling re-launches instances into the same network-partitioned AZ): the same NLB + EC2 ASG + Aurora Multi-AZ base, with the ASG registered for ARC zonal shift (AvailabilityZoneImpairmentPolicy). Deploy-verified, in the same live infrastructure, both with and without an active operator-triggered zonal shift: without it, the replacement lands back in the same broken AZ (reproducing G-2); with ReplaceUnhealthy active, it lands in the healthy AZ instead.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Agentic Code Review Gate for ECS Fargate CI/CD (ecspresso + CodePipeline)
item.description: A CodeCommit/CodePipeline CI/CD reference for ECS Fargate that adds an Amazon Bedrock agentic code review gate between Build and Deploy: security/infra/quality/cost perspectives are reviewed in parallel against each push's git diff, and the pipeline blocks when the aggregated risk level reaches a configurable threshold. Deploys sample task/service definitions with ecspresso + jsonnet; this workspace has no real ECS cluster/service, so the Deploy stage only runs `ecspresso render` (no AWS API calls).

item.title: Cross-Account CI/CD from a Single CodeCommit Repository
item.description: One CodeCommit repository in the dev account feeding three CodePipelines, each deployed into its own account (dev/stg/prd); only the Source stage crosses accounts, assuming a fixed-name IAM role while EventBridge forwards push events across accounts to trigger each pipeline.

item.title: FIS Chaos: CloudFront + Internal ALB + ECS Fargate + Aurora PostgreSQL
item.description: Four AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for a container-based three-tier web architecture: Aurora writer→reader failover, ECS all-tasks stop (with CloudFront S3 fallback), ECS→DB network blackhole on TCP 5432, and ALB→ECS network blackhole on TCP 80 — each with an ALB 5xx CloudWatch Alarm stop condition.

item.title: FIS Chaos: CloudFront + Internal ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling Group + Aurora PostgreSQL
item.description: Four AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for an EC2-based three-tier web architecture: EC2 instance termination (50% PERCENT), CPU stress via SSM (all instances, 5 min), Aurora writer→reader failover, and EC2→DB network blackhole on TCP port 5432 — each with an ALB 5xx CloudWatch Alarm stop condition.

item.title: FIS Chaos: CloudFront + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB
item.description: Four AWS FIS chaos experiment templates for a serverless CRUD API: DynamoDB internal errors (all ops), write-only throttle, read-only throttle, and Lambda concurrency exhaustion — each with a CloudWatch Alarm stop condition. Uses aws:fis:inject-api-* targeting the Lambda execution role to intercept DynamoDB calls at the control plane without touching function code.

item.title: API Gateway + Single-Purpose Lambda
item.description: A Todos REST API where every API Gateway method is backed by its own narrowly-scoped Lambda function, each with an independent IAM role, log group, bundle, and least-privilege DynamoDB grant (read-only for GET, write-only for POST/DELETE). One of three companion workspaces comparing API Gateway + Lambda integration styles against the same API.

item.title: API Gateway + Lambdalith (Hono)
item.description: The same Todos REST API served by a single Lambda function, with routing done in-process by the Hono framework via its aws-lambda adapter and API Gateway reduced to a thin {proxy+} pass-through. One of three companion workspaces comparing API Gateway + Lambda integration styles against the same API.

item.title: API Gateway + Lambda Web Adapter (Express.js)
item.description: The same Todos REST API served by a single Lambda that runs a standard Express.js HTTP server, with the AWS Lambda Web Adapter layer translating the API Gateway proxy event into a real HTTP request so the identical image also runs on Fargate or a local node process. One of three companion workspaces comparing API Gateway + Lambda integration styles against the same API.

item.title: Route 53 Private Hosted Zone Delegation
item.description: Parent private hosted zone system.example.com delegates dev.system.example.com and stg.system.example.com to two child VPCs using the June 2025 Route 53 Resolver DNS delegation feature (INBOUND_DELEGATION endpoints + DELEGATE resolver rules), with a fourth on-premises-role VPC and all four VPCs joined by one Transit Gateway.

item.title: Route 53 Resolver Inbound/Outbound Endpoints
item.description: A verification VPC with the system.example.com private hosted zone and both a Resolver inbound endpoint (switchable via parameter between the default and the June 2025 INBOUND_DELEGATION type) and outbound endpoint, peered with an on-premises-role VPC running a BIND9 DNS server.

item.title: Multi-VPC Transit Gateway
item.description: Three VPCs (10.0/16, 10.1/16, 10.2/16) joined into a full mesh by one Transit Gateway with a single, explicitly managed TGW route table (association + propagation on every attachment), plus one SSM-managed test instance per VPC for connectivity verification.

item.title: AWS Backup Cross-Region (Tokyo to Osaka)
item.description: A single tag-based AWS Backup Selection protecting a sample EC2 instance, RDS database, S3 bucket, and an entire CloudFormation stack in Tokyo, with every recovery point copied cross-region to a pre-created secondary vault in Osaka.

item.title: ECR Cross-Region Replication
item.description: Amazon ECR cross-region replication from Tokyo to Osaka, with both repositories pre-created and independently lifecycle-managed so the replica keeps its own retention policy instead of inheriting none.

item.title: WAF Log Reporting
item.description: Daily WAF Count/Block activity reports built two ways from the same logs: CloudWatch Logs Insights + Lambda + SNS, and Athena + Lambda + SNS, either against a standalone sample Web ACL or an existing WAF.

item.title: EC2 Dual ENI
item.description: Single EC2 instance with two network interfaces: eth0 for internet-facing HTTP/HTTPS traffic (with Elastic IP), and eth1 for SSH management access restricted to specific CIDRs.

item.title: API Gateway + S3 Stub API
item.description: Build a Lambda-free mock/stub HTTP API by wiring API Gateway directly to S3 via an AWS Service integration, returning canned JSON files.

item.title: SNS Basic Fan-Out Patterns
item.description: A single SNS topic fanned out to Email, SQS, Lambda, HTTPS (API Gateway to S3/DynamoDB) and Firehose subscriptions, plus a CloudWatch Logs to Lambda to SNS to Lambda alerting chain.

item.title: CloudFront S3 Static Website
item.description: A static site served over HTTPS by CloudFront from a fully private S3 bucket (Origin Access Control), with a Content-Security-Policy response-headers policy, SPA-friendly 403/404-to-index rewrites, and an optional cross-region (us-east-1) WAFv2 Web ACL with an IP allow-list and redacted log fields.

item.title: S3 Static Web Site
item.description: The simplest static website on AWS: S3 static website hosting served straight from the bucket website endpoint, with Block Public Access left fully enabled and anonymous access limited to an allow-list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses via an aws:SourceIp bucket policy (auto-detecting the deploying operator's own global IP).

item.title: CI/CD Pipeline for CloudFront & S3
item.description: A CodePipeline/CodeBuild pipeline that builds a static site from CodeCommit and deploys it to S3/CloudFront, with an S3 sync Lambda, an async CloudFront invalidation Lambda driven by the CodePipeline continuation-token pattern, and an opt-in manual approval gate.

item.title: Budgets & Cost Anomaly Detection
item.description: Five FinOps alerting patterns with AWS CDK: threshold-based Budget alerts, ML-based Cost Anomaly Detection, a unified SNS topic with optional Slack delivery, the classic CloudWatch billing alarm, and a scheduled Step Functions cost digest to Slack/Microsoft Teams via AWS Chatbot.

item.title: CloudFront with VPC Origin
item.description: Configure CloudFront distribution with VPC origin using AWS CDK.

item.title: CloudWatch Logs to S3 Archive
item.description: Archive CloudWatch Logs to S3 using AWS CDK.

item.title: EC2 Advanced Patterns
item.description: Four EC2 deployment patterns using AWS CDK: Single Instance, Auto-Recovery, ASG Always-1, and ASG Multi-AZ with ALB. Covers IMDSv2, SSM Session Manager access, CloudWatch alarms, and operational notifications.

item.title: ECS Fargate with ALB
item.description: Build a production-ready container application platform combining ECS Fargate and Application Load Balancer (ALB) using AWS CDK.

item.title: SQS to Lambda to Kinesis Firehose
item.description: Process messages from SQS queue using Lambda function and stream to Kinesis Firehose for data lake storage.

item.title: VPC Peering Connection
item.description: Establish VPC peering connection between two VPCs for private network communication.

item.title: CDK Parameters Best Practices
item.description: Learn how to manage parameters and configurations in AWS CDK applications.

item.title: VPC with NAT Instance
item.description: Create VPC with NAT instance for cost-effective internet access from private subnets.

item.title: VPC Basics with CDK
item.description: Create a basic VPC infrastructure with public and private subnets using AWS CDK.

item.title: IAM Basics with CDK
item.description: Create IAM roles, policies, and users with AWS CDK following best practices.

item.title: S3 Basics with CDK
item.description: Create and configure S3 buckets with various settings using AWS CDK.
